title: SE Enablement: Messaging + Competitive Positioning + Demo Practice

transcript:
Header: 2026-08-10 09:00 PDT | Duration: ~60 min | Attendees: Samir, Lena, Tom, Priya, Marcus, Allison

Summary: Quick internal enablement covering messaging and demo practice. Keep notes brief, this is for SE/AE rehearsal.

00:00 Samir: okay everyone good morning, thanks for joining the enablement, quick agenda \u001f messaging, competitive, demo practice. we'll try to keep this tight to an hour.
00:18 Lena: hi all, i'll kick off with a 5-minute refresher on the top value props we want to land \u001f production-first, cost controls, and deployment flexibility.
00:28 Lena: so the core one-liner we've been using is "Redwood Inference: predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated and private deployments" \u001f short, we might tighten that to, uh, "production-first inference with predictable latency and cost" \u001f feedback?
00:45 Tom: i like the predictable latency piece, customers care about SLOs. can we put more emphasis on cost levers? like batching, kv cache.
00:56 Lena: yes absolutely, call out "cost controls: intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching, and model/quantization recommendations" \u001f helps in buyer convos for teams that are cost-sensitive.
01:12 Priya: i usually mention the routing policies, that helps the product folks see how to set fallbacks between hosted and dedicated variants.
01:24 Marcus: small nit, sometimes people don't know what KV cache is, we should have a one-liner: "KV cache stores recent token state to speed up repeated prompts and reduce tokens sent upstream" \u001f keep it short.
01:40 Samir: cool. now competitive positioning \u001f when customers say "why not OpenAI/Anthropic?" what do we say.
01:48 Lena: top-level: OpenAI/Anthropic are model-first and great for rapid prototyping. our angle is serving: if you need production SLAs, predictable unit economics and private deployment options, we win.
02:02 Samir: emphasize unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private \u001f that's different from people who only have a hosted api or only on-prem.
02:12 Priya: customers ask about model quality parity \u001f they want to know if outputs match GPT-class models. how do we handle that without promising?
02:22 Lena: say: we curate and verify open models and provide performance profiles; recommend model variants tuned for cost vs quality, and we run evals tied to the customer's prompt set so they can see regression alerts. avoid claiming parity, focus on measurable evals.
02:40 Tom: security questions \u001f SOC2, ISO, SSO, SAML, KMS. what are the standard answers?
02:47 Lena: SOC 2 Type II is supported for our hosted product; for Private deployments customers can integrate their KMS or HSM and we provide audit logs and RBAC. use the term "customer-managed keys" not too deep on the crypto.
03:05 Allison: sometimes the transcript or notes show "sock two" in calls (people mishear), we should prep messaging for non-technical execs: "We maintain independent third-party audits for security control".
03:18 Samir: great. demo script \u001f roles: AE intro, SE show infra and perf, AE closes with commercial. we'll roleplay two demos today. Marcus and Lena will do the first.
03:30 Lena: have the demo checklist handy: 1) quick context + pain, 2) architecture sketch (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 3) live perf demo (latency/cost), 4) show failover policy, 5) show console observability (token-level cost).
03:50 Marcus: question on failover demo \u001f how do we simulate capacity fail and show fallback to a cheaper model without breaking the app?
04:00 Lena: we can show the routing policy in the console, then simulate a limited capacity condition in the demo environment to trigger fallback. demo script step: flip policy, show request hitting fallback, and show acceptable degradation. i'll record a short clip.
04:18 Tom: audience sometimes asks about dedicated GPU types and whether we support quantized models. quick answer?
04:26 Lena: yes we support quantized exec paths and recommend quantization profiles per workload; dedicated offers predictable throughput and quantization usually reduces memory and cost with small quality tradeoffs.
04:38 Priya: ok let's run the roleplay now. Marcus (AE role) do your intro.
04:45 Marcus: hi i'm marcus, thanks for the time, quick background \u001f we help product teams reduce inference cost and improve latency. can you share your current stack?
04:56 Tom (playing customer): yep we use a mix \u001f prototype on OpenAI, but for production we run self-hosted on our infra using a mix of GPUs; we're concerned about cost and SLOs.
05:10 Marcus: right, common. we often recommend moving inference to a dedicated pool initially to get predictable throughput then use caching to reduce token costs.
05:21 Lena (SE demo): i'm going to share my screen \u001f architecture slide first... (screen share noises) \u001f here is the routing policy, here's the model catalog, here's the per-route token cost.
05:40 Lena: note the batching configuration suggestions, and down here see the KV cache hits rate, that reduces repeat tokenization.
05:52 Samir: small coaching note \u001f when customers say "self-hosted" ask about SLA needs and audit requirements; that's a handoff to Dedicated or Private.
06:04 Marcus: demo practice feedback: tone down the product-nerd details until they ask, and always tie it back to business metrics (cost per session, latency SLOs).
06:20 Tom: i flubbed the objection on "why not just use our own infra?" how to counter?
06:26 Lena: short answer: build vs buy. you can self-host but you pay hidden SRE and ops costs plus slower iteration; we offer a predictable unit cost and tooling to reduce those ops overheads. use an example: one customer saved ~30% in unit cost after batching and caching tuned.
06:45 Priya: remember to mention model rollouts/automatic fallback so security teams know we don't force a single version in production.
06:55 Samir: good. next quick scenario: security-first buyer asking about data residency and private control plane. Lena take it.
07:05 Lena: for regulated customers we provide Private deployments with a customer-managed control plane or VPC option, and on-prem packaging for air-gapped needs. we integrate with KMS and HSM for key custody and provide audit logs, plus RBAC and SSO via SAML.
07:27 Marcus: someone will ask for SOC2 and a pen test report \u001f standard response: we have SOC2 Type II for hosted, and for Dedicated/Private we support audit evidence and can work with security to scope a contractually required review.
07:45 Samir: ok time to wrap with the second roleplay \u001f this one focuses on Dedicated vs Hosted decision. i'll play the customer.
07:52 Samir (as customer): we need 200 requests/second at p95 < 400ms, can you support that?
08:02 Lena: yes, dedicated pools with configured autoscaling and GPU types can be sized to meet that. we also provide burst capacity and smart routing to fallback models when capacity constraints appear.
08:18 Samir: and cost?
08:21 Lena: we'll show a side-by-side: hosted is lower up-front friction but variable unit cost; Dedicated is predictable monthly committment but lower per-token at scale. we also recommend building a pilot to measure your real token distribution and tune quantization and batching.
08:36 Allison: demo practice note \u001f make the cost example concrete: use a sample per-1M token number for hosted vs dedicated. A number helps.
08:46 Lena: agreed. i'll prepare a sample worksheet they can reuse.
08:52 Tom: transcription funny bits \u001f sometimes "KV" becomes "K V" or "SOC 2" becomes "sock two" in transcripts, don't be thrown off by that.
09:02 Marcus: final feedback from the group: 1) tighten the opening one-liner; 2) prepare a 30-second security script for SOC2/ISO/SSO; 3) Lena to record the failover clip.
09:18 Samir: recap and next steps \u001f samir to send the messaging deck and battlecards, lena to upload demo clip and script, tom to update playbook. We'll run a 30-minute roleplay next Tuesday. Thanks everyone.

End of call.
